claim_reference: Adv. Funct. Mater. 2026, 36:e75639, Section 2.1, SI Section 1, Table S2

preregistration.hypothesis: The 43-row prior dataset from Table S2 provides high-fidelity physical information without severe imputation noise or parameter space degeneracy for surrogate learning.
preregistration.primary_metric: Propagated imputation RMSE divided by soft-regime tolerance window (RMSE / 0.15 kPa) <= 1.0, and ARD lengthscales avoid boundary pegging.
preregistration.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if imputation RMSE <= 0.15 kPa and ARD lengthscales are finite/well-conditioned; WEAKENED if imputation RMSE > 3x tolerance window (>= 0.45 kPa) or severe ARD lengthscale divergence occurs; CONTRADICTED if prior exhibits near-zero feature variance across major components.

summary: Audit of Table S2 prior data reveals two critical pathologies: (1) Modulus E was imputed via Gradient Boosting with nominal R^2=0.80, propagating an RMSE of ~1.43 kPa, which is 9.5x larger than the soft-regime target tolerance (±0.15 kPa). (2) LAP is identically 0.10 wt.% in 81.4% of prior rows and exposure times are restricted to 30/90 s in 67.4% of rows, causing ARD lengthscale divergence on GelMA-L (pegs to upper bound >10.0) and severe parameter degeneracy, distorting initial surrogate priors.
